referents.why: Dative 'to them' is the crowd Pilate questions. The crowd of 15:8 and 15:11 is not offered as a candidate here.
Neuter interrogative 'What' as object of 'do'. It asks which deed is to be done and refers to no candidate; the answer is the action itself.

Relative 'the One' (masculine singular) is Jesus, the person the crowd calls King. Jesus is not offered as a candidate. The candidate King (w13) names the title, not the person, so it does not fit as the referent.
First singular 'What I should do' inside Pilate's question: the speaker is Pilate. The builder's w2 is correct.
Second plural 'you call' inside Pilate's question: the addressees are the crowd, not offered as a candidate.

links.why: The answering participle is part of the saying verb, nested as the grammar nests it.
The relative clause 'you call King' sits inside the question's noun phrase, as a relative clause does.
The question is the said words, nested inside the saying clause.
Self link. The verse opens with the question, so there is no earlier clause within the verse.
The saying clause introduces the question, which is what is said (R1). Kept alongside the turn.

groups.why: The part is the question cl2. The answering participle cl1 is the saying clause, not what is said, so it leaves the part; its speech is carried by the content link. Sender is Pilate. The addressee member is removed because the crowd it would name is not an offered candidate.
groups.category: turn part is the said clause

none_fit.what: Jesus, the referent of 'the One' and of the implied object in this verse, is not offered as a candidate, and neither is the crowd addressed. Both are set to none.
